mainTopic: The חרש and תרומה, a קטן reading the מגילה, and daytime מצוות that are valid from dawn
overview: This amud opens by finishing a question from the previous amud. The question is whose view allows a חרש, who speaks but cannot hear his own words, to separate תרומה even לכתחילה. The גמרא gives two answers. First, it is רבי יהודה's own view, and the stricter ruling he taught elsewhere came from his teacher רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. Second, it may follow רבי מאיר, who holds that the heart's intent is what counts in קריאת שמע. Next, רבי יהודה tries to prove that a קטן may read the מגילה from his own childhood, and so does רבי. The חכמים reject both proofs: a child's testimony is not evidence, and the practice of the one who permits something proves nothing. A new משנה then teaches that the מגילה, מילה, טבילה and הזאה wait for sunrise but are valid from עמוד השחר. The גמרא brings a פסוק for each one, explains that רבי יהושע בן לוי's night reading of the מגילה is a separate reading, and asks why the שומרת יום כנגד יום is listed separately. Its answer, that she needs a ספירה, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: It really is רבי יהודה: one source gives his own view, the other gives his teacher's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תרומה ברייתא does follow רבי יהודה, who allows a חרש even לכתחילה. The ברכת המזון ברייתא, which allows it only בדיעבד, reports the view of his teacher.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, it is רבי יהודה, and he allows it even from the start. And there is no difficulty: this ברייתא is his own view, and that ברייתא is his teacher's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its earlier question. The ברייתא about a חרש separating תרומה follows רבי יהודה after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that רבי יהודה seemed to allow inaudible speech only בדיעבד, based on the ברכת המזון ברייתא. The answer splits the two sources. In the תרומה ברייתא, רבי יהודה states his own view, which allows it even לכתחילה. In the ברכת המזון ברייתא, he is passing on his teacher's view, which requires audible speech לכתחילה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Actually / really': the גמרא keeps its original idea and explains away the problem
From the start; the ideal way to act
'And it is not difficult': introduces a way to settle two sources that seem to clash
'This is his own view, that is his teacher's view'

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יהודה contradicts himself. He sometimes teaches a view that is not his own, passing on what his teacher said.

phrases.english: Actually, it is Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא allowing a חרש to separate תרומה follows him.

phrases.english: and he allows it even from the start.
phrases.notes: Not only after the fact.

phrases.english: And it is not difficult:
phrases.notes: The contradiction with the Grace after Meals ברייתא is resolved.

phrases.english: this one is his own view, that one is his teacher's view.
phrases.notes: The תרומה ruling is his own. The ברכת המזון ruling is his teacher's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised on the previous amud: whose view is the ברייתא of יהודה בריה דרבי שמעון בן פזי?
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the sources: one gives the תנא's own view, the other gives his teacher's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות give רבי יהודה's own view, so he would allow inaudible speech only בדיעבד, and the תרומה ברייתא could not be his.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה himself allows it even לכתחילה. The בדיעבד-only ruling belongs to his teacher, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

steps.title: Proof that רבי יהודה's teacher requires audible קריאת שמע
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה, quoting רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, says קריאת שמע must be audible to one's own ears, based on the word 'שמע'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה that one who reads שמע must make it audible to his own ears. The פסוק says 'Hear, O Israel', meaning: let your ears hear what you say with your mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support its answer. It shows that רבי יהודה did quote his teacher as requiring audible speech.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 claimed that רבי יהודה has a teacher whose view differs from his own. This ברייתא confirms it: רבי יהודה quotes רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. His teacher reads the word 'שמע' as a command to hear one's own words. That is why audible speech is required לכתחילה.

keyTerms.meaning: That he make it audible to his own ear
'As it is said': introduces a פסוק

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Yehuda says
in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya:
phrases.notes: This is his teacher.

phrases.english: One who recites the Shema
must make it audible to his own ear,
as it is said:
"Hear, O Israel, the Lord is our God, the Lord is One"
phrases.notes: דברים ו:ד

phrases.english: meaning: let your ears hear
phrases.notes: The word 'שמע' is read as 'make heard'.

phrases.english: what you bring out of your mouth.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 1's claim that רבי יהודה's teacher requires audible speech.
steps.raayaObject: That 'הא דרביה' is real: רבי יהודה passed on a stricter view from his teacher.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי יהודה quotes רבי אלעזר בן עזריה on קריאת שמע, based on the פסוק 'שמע ישראל'.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: what matters is the intent of the heart
steps.stepSummary: In the same ברייתא, רבי מאיר disagrees. Since the words are to be 'on your heart', the heart's intent is what counts, and hearing is not needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: the פסוק says 'which I command you today shall be on your heart'. The words follow the intent of the heart.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of the same ברייתא. רבי מאיר gives the opposing view: קריאת שמע does not need to be audible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר learns from a different פסוק, 'על לבבך'. For him, what makes the words count is the heart's focus, not one's ears hearing them. This opinion matters in the next step, where the גמרא uses רבי מאיר as a new author for the תרומה ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: The intent or focus of the heart
'Those are the words': the words are defined by the heart's intent

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
"which I command you today, upon your heart"
phrases.notes: דברים ו:ו

phrases.english: after the intent of the heart
go the words.
phrases.notes: The words count based on the heart's intent, not on being heard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא from Step 2 with the opposing opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, קריאת שמע depends on the heart's intent, and it need not be audible to one's ears.

steps.title: Second answer: רבי יהודה follows his teacher, and the תרומה ברייתא follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: Now that this ברייתא has been cited, the גמרא offers a new answer. רבי יהודה may agree with his teacher, and the ברייתא allowing a חרש to separate תרומה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have come to this, you can even say that רבי יהודה agrees with his teacher. And the ברייתא taught by יהודה בריה דרבי שמעון בן פזי follows רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer to the original question about the חרש. It now assigns the ברייתא to רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא just quoted introduced a new opinion, רבי מאיר's, who does not require hearing at all. That opens an easier answer. רבי יהודה need not be split from his teacher: he can hold, like his teacher, that it is valid only בדיעבד. The ruling that a חרש may separate תרומה even לכתחילה fits רבי מאיר's view.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Now that you have come to this': introduces a new answer made possible by what was just said

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for whose view allows a חרש to separate תרומה לכתחילה. (1) רבי יהודה's own view, while the stricter source is his teacher's view. (2) רבי מאיר, who says the heart's intent is what counts, while רבי יהודה agrees with his teacher.

phrases.english: Now that you have come to this,
phrases.notes: Now that the ברייתא with רבי מאיר's view has been quoted.

phrases.english: you can even say that Rabbi Yehuda
holds like his teacher,
phrases.notes: Audible speech is required from the start, but it is valid after the fact.

phrases.english: and that which was taught by

phrases.aramaic: יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי —
phrases.english: Yehuda, son of Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא that a חרש may separate תרומה even from the start.

phrases.english: follows Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָתֵית לְהָכִי אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה כְּרַבֵּיהּ סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי מאיר's opinion from Step 3 to offer a second answer, replacing the split given in Step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the author: the ברייתא is attributed to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא had to be explained as רבי יהודה's own view, different from his teacher's.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה agrees with his teacher, and the ברייתא allowing a חרש לכתחילה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא shows that one ברייתא can be explained in more than one way. A newly quoted source can open a simpler answer.

steps.title: The משנה: רבי יהודה allows a minor to read the מגילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to a new line in the משנה: רבי יהודה rules that a קטן is valid to read the מגילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה rules that a minor is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a new topic. The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling about a קטן to set up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a קטן may not read the מגילה, while רבי יהודה allows it. The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's view so it can bring the ברייתא that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor; a child below the age of מצוות

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda rules that a minor is valid.
phrases.notes: Quoted from the משנה, about a קטן reading the מגילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new topic from the משנה, after finishing the חרש discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a קטן is valid to read the מגילה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's proof: he read the מגילה as a child before the elders of לוד
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה supports his view with a story: as a child, he read the מגילה before רבי טרפון and the זקנים in לוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches, רבי יהודה said: I was a minor, and I read the מגילה before רבי טרפון and the elders in לוד.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה brings a real-life event as proof. The great חכמים let him read as a child, so a קטן must be valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is proof from an action. If רבי טרפון and the elders allowed a child to read the מגילה for them, that shows they held a קטן is valid. The proof depends on רבי יהודה's own memory from childhood.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: in front of, before (a gathering)
Lod, a town where חכמים gathered

phrases.english: (As it is taught:) Rabbi Yehuda said:
I was a minor,
and I read it before Rabbi Tarfon
phrases.notes: 'It' is the מגילה.

phrases.english: and the elders in Lod.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יהודה's proof for the משנה ruling quoted in Step 5.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's ruling that a קטן is valid to read the מגילה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story from his own childhood: he read before רבי טרפון and the elders of לוד, and they accepted it.

steps.title: The חכמים reject the proof: a minor's testimony is not accepted
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that you cannot bring proof from a קטן. רבי יהודה was a child when it happened, so his testimony about it is not reliable.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: one does not bring proof from a minor.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back against רבי יהודה's proof. They do not accept his childhood story as evidence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rejection does not argue about the law of a קטן reading the מגילה. It attacks the evidence itself. רבי יהודה saw the event as a child, and a child's observation does not count as valid testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: One does not bring a proof

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים are not saying רבי יהודה is lying. They are saying a memory from when someone was a קטן is not acceptable proof, even when the person telling it is now a great חכם.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה's proof that a קטן may read the מגילה is rejected, because a child's observation cannot serve as evidence.

phrases.english: They said to him:
One does not bring a proof from a minor.
phrases.notes: He was a minor when it happened, so his report cannot serve as evidence.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֵין מְבִיאִין רְאָיָה מִן הַקָּטָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof (the evidence), not necessarily the ruling itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The witness was a קטן when the event happened, so his report is not valid evidence.

steps.title: רבי's childhood story of reading before רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא: רבי says that as a child he read the מגילה in front of רבי יהודה. This is meant to prove a קטן may read.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי said: I was a child, and I read the מגילה in front of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא with another story meant to prove that a קטן can read the מגילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 brought רבי יהודה's own childhood story. Here, רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא) brings a similar story from his own childhood. Since רבי יהודה let him read, it seems a קטן is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: literally 'above'; here it means 'in front of / before' a great person

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita: Rebbi said:
I was a minor, and I read it (the Megillah)
before Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: literally 'above רבי יהודה'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel proof story, after the first one (step 6) was rejected in step 7
steps.raayaObject: That a קטן is valid to read the מגילה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי's testimony that רבי יהודה let him read as a child

steps.title: No proof from the one who permits it
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reject רבי's proof: רבי יהודה already holds a קטן is valid, so of course he let a child read.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: You cannot bring a proof from the very person who permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push away רבי's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה already rules that a קטן may read. So when he lets a child read, he is just following his own opinion. That tells us nothing about whether the other חכמים agree.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not bring a proof

steps.confusionAlert: This is a different rejection from step 7. There the problem was 'you were a child.' Here the problem is 'רבי יהודה is the one who permits it.'

phrases.english: They said to him:
One does not bring a proof from the one who permits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֵין מְבִיאִין רְאָיָה מִן הַמַּתִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 8
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof only; it does not decide the הלכה about a קטן
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A person's practice that follows his own ruling cannot prove that ruling is correct

steps.title: Why not say 'you were a child'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the חכמים did not also tell רבי, as they told רבי יהודה, that a child's testimony is no proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them say to him: You cannot bring a proof from a child!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the rejection in step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי was also a child when it happened, just like רבי יהודה in step 6. So the simpler rejection from step 7 should have worked here too. Why did the חכמים use a different argument?

keyTerms.meaning: And let them say to him

phrases.english: And let them say to him:
One does not bring a proof from a minor!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵימְרוּ לֵיהּ: אֵין מְבִיאִין רְאָיָה מִן הַקָּטָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the choice of rejection in step 9
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'you were a child' argument from step 7 seems to fit here too. So why was it not used?

steps.title: They gave two reasons
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים actually said both: you were a child, and even if you had been an adult, there is no proof from the one who permits.
steps.simpleTranslation: They told him one thing and then another. First: you were a child. And also: even if you had been an adult, you cannot bring a proof from the one who permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the חכמים used both arguments at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'you were a child' reason was said too. The ברייתא just highlights the extra reason. Even if an adult had testified to seeing a child read before רבי יהודה, it would prove nothing, because רבי יהודה was only following his own view.

keyTerms.meaning: One thing, and more (a two-part argument)

steps.whatToRemember: Both childhood proof-stories fail. A child's testimony is not reliable. And רבי יהודה acting on his own view proves nothing about the הלכה.

phrases.english: They told him one thing and another.
One: that you were a minor,
and furthermore: even if you had been an adult —
one does not bring a proof from the one who permits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both arguments were said; the ברייתא quotes the additional one
steps.terutzMaskana: They used it too, and added a second, stronger argument

steps.title: Daytime מצוות: wait for sunrise, but valid from dawn
steps.stepSummary: New משנה: the מגילה, מילה, טבילה, הזאה, and the טבילה of a שומרת יום כנגד יום are done only after sunrise. But if done from עמוד השחר, they are valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not read the מגילה, do a ברית מילה, immerse, or sprinkle purifying water until sunrise. So too, a שומרת יום כנגד יום should not immerse until sunrise. But for all of them, if done from dawn on, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists מצוות that belong to the daytime.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ideally, we wait until הנץ החמה (sunrise) to be safe. But after the fact, from עמוד השחר it already counts as day, so these acts are כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who had non-menstrual bleeding and must wait one clean day
Sprinkle the purifying water (of the פרה אדומה)

phrases.english: MISHNA: One does not read the Megillah,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא מָלִין, וְלֹא טוֹבְלִין, וְלֹא מַזִּין,
phrases.english: nor circumcise, nor immerse, nor sprinkle,
and likewise a woman who watches a day for a day —
she may not immerse until the sun rises.
And all of them that were done
from when dawn broke — are valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה; new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Daytime מצוות should wait for sunrise, but are valid from עמוד השחר

steps.title: Source for daytime reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that the מגילה is read by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants a פסוק showing that reading the מגילה is tied to the daytime.

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for reading the מגילה by day

steps.title: The verse says 'these days'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'והימים האלה נזכרים ונעשים' says 'days,' so the reading is by day and not at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the פסוק says: 'And these days are remembered and kept.' By day, yes; at night, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק from מגילת אסתר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'days' (ימים) is read to mean daytime. So the 'remembering' (the reading) is done by day.

phrases.english: For the verse says:
'And these days are remembered and kept' —
by day, yes; at night, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'days' in the פסוק limits the reading to daytime

steps.title: Does this refute רבי יהושע בן לוי?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי says one must read the מגילה at night and again by day. 'Not at night' seems to contradict him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a refutation of רבי יהושע בן לוי? For רבי יהושע בן לוי said: A person must read the מגילה at night and read it again by day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהושע בן לוי from the משנה and the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה and the פסוק say 'by day, not at night,' then a night reading seems invalid. But רבי יהושע בן לוי requires a night reading.

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a refutation
of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
for Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: חַיָּיב אָדָם לִקְרוֹת אֶת הַמְּגִילָּה בַּלַּיְלָה
phrases.english: A person is obligated to read the Megillah at night
and to repeat it by day!

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא תֶּיהְוֵי תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the source from step 14 to challenge an אמורא
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן לוי's requirement of a night reading
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'By day, not at night' appears to rule out any night reading

steps.title: The משנה is about the daytime reading
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is only speaking about the daytime reading: it must not be done before dawn. The night reading is a separate obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the משנה teaches this, it is referring to the daytime reading.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge and saves רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה means that the daytime reading cannot be done during the night. It does not deny that there is also a separate night reading. So there is no contradiction.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two readings: one at night and one by day. The משנה's 'only by day, from dawn' rule applies to the daytime reading.
steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not mean there is no night reading at all. It only means the day reading cannot be done at night.

phrases.english: When it teaches this — it refers to the daytime reading.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה rules out any reading at night
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה only sets the time for the daytime reading; the night reading stands

steps.title: Source for doing circumcision by day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the source that מילה is done by day: 'And on the eighth day he shall be circumcised.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And we do not circumcise (before sunrise), etc.' Why? Because it is written: 'And on the eighth DAY he shall be circumcised.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה, מילה, and gives a פסוק showing it must be done by day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as the מגילה source in Step 14. The word 'day' (יום) in the פסוק shows that daytime is required, so מילה is not done at night.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: And we do not circumcise, etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה: not before sunrise.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And on the eighth day he shall be circumcised.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא יב:ג. The key word is 'day.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the מגילה (Steps 13-16) to the next item in the משנה's list, asking the same unstated question: where is it learned from?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Implied: what is the source that מילה is done only by day?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'וביום השמיני ימול' says 'day,' so מילה is done by day.

steps.title: Source for doing sprinkling and immersion by day
steps.stepSummary: הזאה must be by day because the פסוק says 'on the seventh day.' טבילה is linked to הזאה through a היקש, so it also must be by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And we do not immerse and we do not sprinkle (before sunrise), etc.' Why? Because it is written: 'And the pure person shall sprinkle on the impure person... on the seventh DAY.' And immersion is compared to sprinkling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the next two items in the משנה: הזאה (sprinkling) and טבילה (immersion).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק directly says הזאה is 'on the seventh day,' so sprinkling needs daytime. The same פסוק also mentions bathing, so the גמרא says טבילה is 'compared' (היקש) to הזאה. That means טבילה follows the same daytime rule.

keyTerms.meaning: We sprinkle (the purifying waters of the פרה אדומה)
Is compared / linked (a היקש: two things placed together in a פסוק share the same law)

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק itself only says 'day' about the sprinkling. The daytime rule for immersion is not stated directly. It comes from the היקש that links טבילה to הזאה.

phrases.english: And we do not immerse and we do not sprinkle, etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And the pure one shall sprinkle on the impure one
phrases.notes: במדבר יט:יט

phrases.english: [etc.] on the seventh day,'
phrases.notes: The word 'day' shows sprinkling must be by day.

phrases.english: And immersion is compared to sprinkling.
phrases.notes: Both appear in the same פסוק, so they share the daytime rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא טוֹבְלִין וְלֹא מַזִּין וְכוּ׳. דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the item-by-item search for sources, now for הזאה and טבילה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Implied: what is the source that הזאה and טבילה are done only by day?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הזאה: 'ביום השביעי' says day. טבילה: it is linked to הזאה by a היקש.

steps.title: Why mention the day-for-day woman separately?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists שומרת יום כנגד יום separately. The גמרא asks why, since she is just one more person who needs טבילה, and the משנה already said טבילה waits for day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And so too, a שומרת יום כנגד יום may not immerse until the sun rises, etc.' This is obvious! How is a שומרת יום כנגד יום different from everyone else who needs to immerse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's wording. It asks why the משנה needed to list the שומרת יום כנגד יום at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already said that no one immerses before day. A שומרת יום כנגד יום is a woman who saw blood outside her regular נדה time and must wait one clean day before immersing. Her immersion should already be included in that general rule, so mentioning her looks repetitive.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who saw blood during the days between her נדה periods and must 'watch' one clean day for each day she saw
It is obvious! (a challenge that something did not need to be said)

phrases.english: And so too, a woman who watches a day for a day
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא תִּטְבּוֹל עַד שֶׁתָּנֵץ הַחַמָּה וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: may not immerse until the sun rises, etc.
It is obvious!
phrases.notes: The challenge begins.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא שׁוֹמֶרֶת יוֹם כְּנֶגֶד יוֹם
phrases.english: What is different about a woman who watches a day for a day
from all those obligated in immersions!
phrases.notes: She should already be covered by 'ולא טובלין.'

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא! מַאי שְׁנָא שׁוֹמֶרֶת יוֹם כְּנֶגֶד יוֹם מִכׇּל חַיָּיבֵי טְבִילוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 18 showed that all טבילה must be by day. This step asks why the משנה then singles out the שומרת יום כנגד יום.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's separate mention of שומרת יום כנגד יום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The general rule 'ולא טובלין' already covers every immersion, so a separate clause for her seems unnecessary.

steps.title: We might have compared her to a זב's first sighting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the clause was needed. Without it, we might have treated her like the first sighting of a זב, which is linked to a בעל קרי. A בעל קרי immerses on the same day, so she would too.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought she is like the first sighting of a זב. And the first sighting of a זב is compared to a בעל קרי, as it is written: 'This is the law of the זב, and of the one from whom semen goes out.' Just as a בעל קרי immerses on that day, this one too should immerse on her day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by explaining what we might have mistakenly thought (a סלקא דעתך). This passage is setting up the answer. The conclusion of why she still must wait for sunrise comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chain of reasoning has three links. (1) A שומרת יום כנגד יום resembles a זב's first sighting, since one sighting does not yet make a full זב. (2) The פסוק places a זב next to a בעל קרי, linking them. (3) A בעל קרי immerses on the same day as his emission. So we might have thought she may immerse 'on her day,' without waiting for sunrise. That is why the משנה had to spell out her case.

keyTerms.meaning: It would have entered your mind to say (introduces a mistaken assumption)
The first sighting (emission) of a זב
A man who had a seminal emission

steps.confusionAlert: This is only what we WOULD have thought (סלקא דעתך). It is not the final הלכה. The משנה's actual ruling is that she must wait until sunrise.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא: a clause that looks unnecessary is explained by pointing to a mistaken comparison it is meant to block.

phrases.english: It was necessary:
phrases.notes: Start of the answer.

phrases.english: It would have entered your mind to say
phrases.notes: The mistaken assumption begins.

phrases.english: that she should be like the first sighting of a זב —
phrases.notes: One sighting does not yet make a full זב.

phrases.aramaic: וּרְאִיָּה רִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁל זָב אִיתַּקַּשׁ לְבַעַל קֶרִי,
phrases.english: and the first sighting of a זב is compared to a man who had a seminal emission,
as it is written: 'This is the law of the זב
phrases.notes: ויקרא טו:לב

phrases.english: and of the one from whom semen goes out.'
phrases.notes: The two are placed together in the פסוק, so they are linked.

phrases.english: Just as a בעל קרי immerses on that day —
phrases.notes: He immerses on the same day as his emission.

phrases.english: this one too should immerse on her day.
phrases.notes: The mistaken conclusion. The גמרא's correction follows next.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'פשיטא' challenge of Step 19 by showing that a mistaken comparison would otherwise have been possible.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Necessity (איצטריך): the clause blocks a mistaken comparison.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: She is like a זב's first sighting, which is linked to a בעל קרי, who immerses on the same day. So she could immerse on her day without waiting for sunrise.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה mentions her to show she still must wait for sunrise. The full explanation continues next.

steps.title: Refining the mistaken idea: she cannot immerse by day, but maybe she can at night
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sharpens the הוה אמינא from Step 20. A פסוק shows that the שומרת יום כנגד יום cannot immerse on the day she saw blood. Still, we might have thought she could watch part of the following night and then immerse at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, it is true that this woman cannot immerse during the day she saw blood, because the פסוק says, 'All the days of her issue shall be to her like the bed of her נדה.' But at least at night, we might have said, she should watch for part of the night, see that it is clean, and then immerse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still explaining what we would have wrongly thought without the משנה's extra clause. It narrows the comparison to the בעל קרי: same-day immersion is impossible for her, but a nighttime immersion still seems possible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 compared her to a בעל קרי, who immerses on the same day. Here the גמרא admits that this comparison fails for the daytime, because 'כל ימי זובה' makes her whole day of bleeding impure. So the הוה אמינא moves to the night: after a short clean stretch (מקצת שימור), she would immerse without waiting for morning.

keyTerms.meaning: 'All the days of her issue,' the פסוק showing that her day of bleeding is entirely impure
Partial watching: checking that part of a period passed with no bleeding

steps.confusionAlert: This is NOT the גמרא's conclusion. Everything here is still the mistaken idea (הוה אמינא) that the משנה comes to reject.

phrases.english: And although this one cannot immerse by day,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the שומרת יום כנגד יום. 'By day' means the same day she saw blood.

phrases.english: as it is written: 'All the days of her issue
phrases.notes: ויקרא ט״ו:כ״ו

phrases.english: shall be to her as the bed of her menstruation,'
phrases.notes: The entire day of bleeding stays impure, so she cannot immerse during it.

phrases.aramaic: בְּלֵילְיָא מִיהַת לֶיעְבֵּיד מִקְצָת שִׁימּוּר, וְתִיטְבּוֹל,
phrases.english: at least at night she should do a partial watching, and immerse,
phrases.notes: This is the הוה אמינא: wait a little into the night, see that it is clean, and immerse then.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the תירוץ of Step 20. It limits the בעל קרי comparison and moves the הוה אמינא from same-day immersion to nighttime immersion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the הוה אמינא (what we would have mistakenly thought)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: She could watch part of the night after her day of bleeding and then immerse that same night.
steps.terutzMaskana: Given in the next step: the משנה rejects this, because she needs ספירה.

steps.title: The משנה teaches that her counting requirement makes her wait
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins the real answer. The משנה lists her separately to teach that, since she must count a clean day (ספירה), she cannot immerse at night. The reasoning finishes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the משנה comes to teach us: since she needs a counting...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the payoff of the extra clause in the משנה. It begins explaining why a nighttime immersion does not work for her, and the sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key fact is that a שומרת יום כנגד יום needs a ספירה, meaning she must count a clean day after her day of bleeding. A short clean stretch of the night is not enough. This explains why the משנה had to mention her even though it had already said that טבילה waits for day.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It teaches us': the formula that tells what a teaching adds
Counting: the clean day she must count before immersing

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is cut off here. Its ending, that counting must be done by day, comes on the next amud.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows why the משנה's list is not repetitive. The שומרת יום כנגד יום needs her own mention, because her counting requirement is a separate reason she must wait for day.

phrases.english: it teaches us
phrases.notes: This is what the משנה's separate mention of her comes to teach.

phrases.english: that since she requires counting,
phrases.notes: Continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן כֵּיוָן דְּבָעֲיָא סְפִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the nighttime הוה אמינא of Step 21 and gives the reason the משנה needed the clause.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכא: the clause is needed to teach a new detail
steps.terutzHavaAmina: She could immerse at night after a partial watching.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since she requires ספירה, she must wait. The full reason finishes on the next amud.
